brief: Greek Revival white frame village church of the 1840s: a gable-front clapboard nave with a full pediment, corner pilasters, a central door and tall 12/12 windows, and a square belfry tower rising from the front of the roof with a louvred octagonal belfry stage and a tall slender spire. HABS drawings record the building.

facade.notes: Merton Baptist Church (Merton WI, 1845), HABS: a white clapboard Greek Revival gable-front with a full pediment, corner pilasters, a tall panelled door between two big 20-pane windows, a square belfry stage and an octagonal louvred lantern under a spire

why.note: Yankee settlers carried the New England meetinghouse into Wisconsin: a temple front with a steeple on the gable
